correctness.rationale: The unitary Zak transform for M_m T_n g with integer modulation/translation diagonalizes the union of two translated critical lattices with scalar fiber |Zg(x,omega)|^2+|Zg(x-delta,omega)|^2, rather than an irregular-modulation model. Fourier transform of g_w=(t^2+w^2)^-1 equals pi/w exp(-2pi w |xi|), giving the exact squared Zak formula with q=exp(-2pi w). The hyperbolic decomposition shows minima in omega at 1/2 and maxima at omega=0. The minimum spatial envelope is C phi(cos theta), with phi=(1+t)/(2(a-bt)^2) strictly increasing and convex. Jensen plus the cosine-midpoint inequality is ATTAINED at x=(1+delta)/2 or delta/2, giving the exact sharp A_w(delta), strictly maximal at half stagger. The upper envelope E/D(x)^2 at half stagger is maximized at cos=+/-1, yielding B_w(1/2)=pi^2/w^2(coth^2(pi w)+tanh^2(pi w)); evaluating at x=0 shows strict inequality B(delta)>B(1/2) for other delta. The small-delta Taylor expansion gives the stated nonzero d^2 coefficient, while upper bound tends to twice the peak. I independently checked sample values (w=.7: A(1/2)=.9663985874, B(1/2)=40.3328638134), not used as continuum proof.
residual_risks: At arbitrary delta the optimal upper bound is a spatial maximization, not claimed as a general elementary closed form.
At delta=0 or1 the coalescing cosets have zero lower bound; frame assertion is for 0<delta<1 only.
